rules.title: Anti-Eviction Act rent increase limits
rules.requirement: Before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must serve a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.key_value: rent increase must not be unconscionable
rules.summary_plain: Your landlord must give you proper notice before raising your rent, and the increase cannot be unreasonably high.
rules.summary_plain_es: Su arrendador debe darle un aviso adecuado antes de aumentar su renta, y el aumento no puede ser irrazonablemente alto.
rules.coverage_conditions_text: Applies to all rental properties subject to eviction and rent increase laws in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions_text: Publicly financed and subsidized housing developments owned or subsidized by HUD or NJHMFA are not subject to municipal rent control ordinances.
rules.quoted_span: before an owner can evict a tenant for nonpayment of an increased rent, they must first serve the tenant with a valid notice to quit and notice of rent increase. This notice does not mean that the tenant must actually leave; the tenant has the right to remain as long as they pay any legal increase in rent. The increase in rent must not be unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
